record.original_question: Let X be a Banach space that does not contain a copy of ℓ_1, and let ν be an X-valued vector measure whose integration operator I_ν: L^1(ν) → X is completely continuous. Must ν have finite variation?

evidence.quote: Problem 4.4 (Okada - Ricker - Rodríguez-Piazza, [99]). Let X be a Banach space not containing ℓ_1 and let ν be an X-valued vector measure such that I_ν is completely continuous. Does ν have finite variation?

Let $X$ be a real Banach space that does not contain an isomorphic copy of $\ell^1$. Let $(\Omega,\Sigma)$ be a measurable space and let $
u:\Sigma	o X$ be a countably additive vector measure. Recall that a $\Sigma$-measurable scalar function $f$ is integrable with respect to $
u$ (in the sense of Bartle–Dunford–Schwartz) if it is integrable with respect to every scalar measure $\langle 
u,x^*angle$, $x^*\in X^*$, and if for every $A\in\Sigma$ there exists an element $\int_A f\,d
u\in X$ such that $\langle \int_A f\,d
u,\,x^*angle=\int_A f\,d\langle
u,x^*angle$ for all $x^*\in X^*$. The space $L^1(
u)$ of (equivalence classes of) such integrable functions is a Banach lattice under the norm $\|f\|_
u=\sup_{\|x^*\|\le 1}\int|f|\,d|\langle
u,x^*angle|$, and the integration operator $I_
u:L^1(
u)	o X$ is defined by $I_
u(f)=\int_\Omega f\,d
u$. The variation of $
u$ is $|
u|(\Omega)=\sup\sum_i\|
u(A_i)\|$, the supremum being taken over all finite measurable partitions of $\Omega$; $
u$ is said to have finite variation when $|
u|(\Omega)<\infty$. A bounded linear operator between Banach spaces is completely continuous (Dunford–Pettis) if it maps weakly convergent sequences to norm convergent sequences.

Question: Under the assumption that $X$ contains no copy of $\ell^1$ and that $I_
u:L^1(
u)	o X$ is completely continuous, must $
u$ necessarily have finite variation?

status_evidence.title: Operator ideal properties of vector measures with finite variation
status_evidence.snippet: Studies relationships between finite variation of vector measures and operator-ideal properties of the associated integration operators.
status_evidence.claim: Closely related work studies the link between finite variation and ideal properties of $I_\nu$, but does not state a resolution of this specific implication.

status_evidence.title: Lp-spaces and ideal properties of integration operators for Fréchet-space-valued measures
status_evidence.snippet: Investigates compactness, weak compactness and complete continuity of integration operators associated with vector measures.
status_evidence.claim: Treats complete continuity of $I_\nu$ in related settings without establishing the desired finite-variation conclusion under the absence of $\ell^1$.
